question.problem: Given that $X∼B(8,0.3),$ compute $P(X>2).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(8,0.3),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{x})(0.3)^{x}(0.7)^{8-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X>2)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=3,4,…,8.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X\le 2)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,2,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X\le 2),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =P(X\in \{0,1,2\}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{0})(0.3)^{0}(0.7)^{8-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{1})(0.3)^{1}(0.7)^{8-1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{2})(0.3)^{2}(0.7)^{8-2} \\  & =(0.7)^{8}+8(0.3)(0.7)^{7}+28(0.3)^{2}(0.7)^{6} \\  & ≈0.5518\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>2) & =1-P(X\le 2) \\  & ≈1-0.5518 \\  & =0.4482\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.
